sampling_model.design: A two-arm randomized vaccine trial is combined with an external exposure-surveillance sample from the same period-specific target environment.
sampling_model.units: For each trial arm, conditional on that arm's own realized total, the mutually exclusive categories consisting of no first infection and first infection by period and variant have the stated multinomial law. For each period-specific external total, exposure counts on \(\mathcal V_0\) have the stated multinomial law. No independence among the two trial-arm blocks and two external-period blocks is required: each block's exact error bound is first averaged over its own possibly random total, and a union bound gives simultaneous coverage unconditionally over the trial and external samples. No joint conditional coverage claim given the realized trial arm sizes is made.
sampling_model.treatment: \(A\in\{0,1\}\) has known probabilities \(\pi\), and the trial records the period and variant of each first infection.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment-arm positivity is standard. Noninfecting-exposure priming is indexed by the disclosed sensitivity value \(\delta\), with \(\delta=0\) giving no priming and \(\delta=1\) permitting unrestricted priming. Fiber-wide period-two vaccine reference-risk positivity is a separate novel, LP-checkable restriction used only for finite Charnes--Cooper endpoints; the extended identified set and exact projection allow zero denominators.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The trial and exposure cell probabilities are covered by exact likelihood-ratio-ordered multinomial inversions at Bonferroni level \(\alpha/4\) for each of two arms and two periods. At total count zero, \(T_p(0)=0\) and \(\Gamma_0(u;\gamma)=\Delta\), so zero-total and zero-cell samples require no correction. The simultaneous primitive confidence set is projected through every nonempty candidate fiber. Because \(\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\) is nested in \(\delta\), whole-set coverage over a prespecified nonempty closed \(\mathcal D\) reduces exactly to projection through its largest admissible value \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\); no continuum union or closure is needed. The simultaneous guarantee is unconditional over the trial and external samples, uses no independence among count blocks, and does not studentize or select an endpoint optimizer.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 derives sharp two-period bounds for a single-pathogen challenge effect from conventional vaccine-trial risks.
Section 4 shows that multi-variant vaccine-effectiveness measures can be time-varying under leaky and all-or-none mechanisms.
The weighted estimating-equation model permits time-varying vaccine efficacy and time-varying pathogen distributions under a marked exposure process.
Case-only strain odds ratios receive a biological relative-efficacy interpretation under stated exposure and susceptibility conditions.
Theorems 1 through 3 identify conditional relative strain efficacy from case-only data under explicit missingness and causal assumptions.
Finite latent response types and linear programming yield tight treatment-effect bounds and attaining distributions.
The paper constructs random regions with uniform asymptotic coverage of an entire identified set or its known image.
Calibrated bootstrap projection gives uniformly valid intervals for smooth functions of moment-constrained partially identified parameters.
Derivative-aware resampling is valid for directionally differentiable maps in settings where the ordinary bootstrap can fail.
The paper develops a powerful single-pathogen test of treatment-effect constancy and additional waning bounds.

Section 5 defines the marginal time-to-event challenge subtype effect, and the marginal-identification proposition identifies it as a ratio of two observed cause-specific hazard ratios under the paper's stated time-to-event identification and proportionality assumptions.

body.tldr: Changing pathogen variants make early-versus-late vaccine challenge risk depend on one latent coupling of exposures and responses across periods. The response type permits a noninfecting period-one exposure to alter later controlled susceptibility, and \(\delta\in[0,1]\) bounds the altered fraction. The compatible full-law classes, reduced fibers, and sharp extended ratio sets are nested in \(\delta\); hence every nonempty closed sensitivity range \(\mathcal D\) equals its single maximal fiber at \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\), without a closure or continuum supremum. Explicit opposite-side feasibility programs yield attained sharp priming-breakdown points, dual sign certificates below each threshold, and compatible counterlaws at each finite threshold. Reciprocal endpoints remain attained under the separate denominator condition. For \(K=2\), the Janvin--Stensrud and Perényi--Stensrud links are projection/calibration comparisons, not model-class inclusions. Exact multinomial inversion with \(\Gamma_0(u;\gamma)=\Delta\) gives unconditional whole-set coverage, and nesting reduces every prespecified range-coverage audit to \(\bar\delta\). External exposure margins remain primitives and are not replaced by case-strain frequencies.

project_justification.gap: Janvin and Stensrud (2025) give sharp single-pathogen challenge-effect bounds, and Perényi and Stensrud (2025, Section 5) identify a variant-specific time-to-event challenge subtype effect under their exposure and proportionality restrictions. Neither supplies the present sharp common-history ratio set from trial first-infection risks plus external variant-exposure margins when a prior noninfecting exposure may alter later controlled susceptibility. Their results also do not establish the sensitivity nesting that collapses an entire closed priming range to its largest admissible value or the attained opposite-sign breakdown frontier derived here. These are projection/calibration comparisons only, not claims of class inclusion or transfer.
project_justification.niche: The target compares one policy-fixed reference mixture across periods and defines period-two challenge risk after no period-one exposure. A history-indexed response array separates that target response from the response after a noninfecting exposure, while \(\delta\) restricts their disagreement without substituting selected case-strain frequencies for external exposure margins. Because the restriction relaxes monotonically in \(\delta\), a scientifically justified nonempty closed range \(\mathcal D\) has the exact least-favorable endpoint \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\). Routine negative tests and serial serology do not justify a small \(\delta\), so analysis without a controlled validation substudy uses \(\bar\delta=1\).
project_justification.fill: The substantive chain gives exact common-history compression, an always-defined extended sharp set, finite attained reciprocal endpoints under the disclosed denominator condition, and a common-law sign dual. It further proves direct nesting of the compatible laws, fibers, and sharp sets; exact equality of every closed sensitivity-range model with the single \(\bar\delta\) model; and explicit attained lower- and upper-sign priming-breakdown programs. Below a finite threshold the sign dual certifies robustness, while at the threshold exact history compression supplies a compatible counterlaw. For \(K=2\), finite programs compute the projection/calibration boundary to the Perényi--Stensrud observed contrast; the single-variant inequality is likewise a calibration projection to the Janvin--Stensrud geometry, not a class inclusion. Exact primitive-cell multinomial inversion projects through the maximal nonempty fiber, yielding unconditional whole-set coverage for the entire prespecified range.

body.related_work: Janvin and Stensrud (2025, Theorem 1 and Appendix B) establish sharp finite single-pathogen two-period challenge-effect bounds and attaining laws. The present \(K=1\), no-priming inequality is a projection/calibration result recovering their survivor-selection geometry; it is not a model-class inclusion or a transfer of their theorem. Perényi and Stensrud (2025, Section 5 and the marginal \(CSE_k\) identification proposition) identify a time-to-event challenge subtype effect from observed cause-specific hazards under their stated time-to-event exchangeability, positivity, consistency, exposure necessity, no cross-infectivity, covariate-invariant exposure-ratio, and scaled-new-infection proportionality conditions. Here their controlled-risk coordinates are projected from \(\rho_{ta}(x,e^{(v)})\), with the period-two coordinate based on \(R^{[0]}_{2av}\); the affine-hull quadratic test and observed-value equality form an exact projection/calibration boundary, not a claim that either paper's model class contains the other. Tomer and Biccler (2022) analyze temporal movement under specified competing-variant mechanisms. Follmann and Huang (2018), Gilbert et al. (2001), Edlefsen (2014), and van der Laan and Gilbert (2023) explain why selected infecting strains require extra exposure and susceptibility restrictions, so case frequencies are not substituted for the external margins \(q\). Balke and Pearl (1997) inform the finite response-type lift. Romano and Shaikh (2010) and Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) inform whole-set projection; the present exact multinomial construction includes \(\Gamma_0(u;\gamma)=\Delta\), obtains simultaneous unconditional coverage by a union bound without block independence, and uses sensitivity nesting to reduce the full closed-range audit to \(\bar\delta\).
body.technical_internal_limitation: The parameter \(\delta\) controls whether a period-one exposure that did not infect changes the period-two controlled response relative to no prior exposure. Routine negative tests establish noninfection, not absence of immune priming, and serial serology need not detect response-relevant cellular or mucosal changes; neither identifies a small \(\delta\). Without a randomized or controlled validation substudy, the honest range is \(\mathcal D=[0,1]\), and nesting makes its exact least-favorable endpoint \(\bar\delta=1\). The sharp breakdown point is an identified-law feasibility frontier conditional on the maintained common-history model and external margins, not a validation estimate of the biological priming fraction. The finite map still abstracts from multiple distinct noninfecting exposures within one period.
body.honest_scope: Exact common-history projection, the unconditional extended sharp set, finite attained reciprocal endpoints under the separately disclosed fiber-wide denominator condition, and common-history sign separation hold pointwise in prespecified \(\delta\). The new range theorem proves nesting only within this paper's own sensitivity-indexed class: for nonempty closed \(\mathcal D\), its law union, reduced-fiber union, sharp ratio set, uniform sign audit, and whole-set coverage audit reduce exactly to \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\). It does not assert inclusion in, inclusion of, or theorem transfer from the Janvin--Stensrud or Perényi--Stensrud model classes; those links are projection/calibration results. The target period-two risk uses \(R^{[0]}_{21v}\), while observed period-two infections use \(R^{[H_1]}_{2av}\); their discrepancy among noninfected exposees is bounded rather than suppressed. Each finite sign-breakdown threshold is attained and has a compatible counterlaw, but its scientific relevance is limited by external validation of \(\delta\). For \(K=2\), collapse to the observed hazard contrast additionally requires observed positivity, positive controlled-risk-face feasibility, the affine-hull quadratic identity, and equality of its constant with the observed value. External exposure margins remain primitives; pooled case-strain frequencies do not replace them.
